clue.text: Dip asparagus top in watered-down tzatziki finally

indicators.note: the asparagus tip is placed in the word for watered-down

parts.note: watered-down means thin, diluted

indicators.note: the top of a down word is its first letter, so this takes the opening letter of asparagus
finally picks the closing letter of tzatziki

explanation.surface: A recipe tip: dunk the end of an asparagus spear into a thinned-out tzatziki.
explanation.definitionFit: Tahini is a sesame paste served as a dip, a familiar example of one in Middle Eastern cooking.

clue.text: Perhaps Mum accepts post coming up for debating group

indicators.note: the parent word accepts, or takes in, the reversed post

parts.note: Mum is an example of a parent, flagged by perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word for post is read from bottom to top

parts.note: post means mail

explanation.surface: Mum takes delivery of a letter heading for the debating society.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliament is a legislative assembly where members debate and pass laws.

clue.text: Devil's home work almost finished with enthusiasm

indicators.note: a word almost finished loses its final letter

parts.note: a task is a piece of work
a mania is a craze, an intense enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Someone nearly done with a job, throwing themselves at it with gusto, as if the devil drove them.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tasmanian devil is a marsupial found in the wild only on this Australian island state, so the 'Devil' is an animal, not Satan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tasmanian devil, a carnivorous marsupial, lives only on this island, which is therefore its habitat.

clue.text: Student butts in to denounce programme

indicators.note: the student letter butts in, pushing itself into the middle of the word for denounce

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, to denounce
L is the learner driver's plate, standing for a student

explanation.surface: A student interrupts to condemn a television programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme of intended actions, the same as a programme of things to be done.

clue.text: Uncompromising Dad heard out when he interrupts

indicators.note: the word he interrupts the rearranged letters by sitting among them
out signals the letters of Dad heard are put out of order

explanation.surface: A stubborn father has caught wind of things and his son butts in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dad heard' reads as the subject of a sentence, but the two words are only the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-headed describes someone practical and unyielding, not swayed by sentiment, so uncompromising.

clue.text: Wearing best suit maybe, but hurt

definitions.meaning: first meaning: smartly dressed, well turned out
second meaning: to sting or feel pain

explanation.surface: Someone dressed up for an occasion who is nonetheless in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means neatly and stylishly dressed; the verb means to sting or ache.

clue.text: It's painful when penny's pinched from pocket!

indicators.note: pinched means stolen, so the penny is taken out of the word for pocket

parts.note: a pouch is a small pocket or bag
P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: A cry of distress on finding a pickpocket has lifted your coins.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what someone cries out when something hurts them.

clue.text: Eccentrics when potting Red, Green, Blue and Black?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: strange or unconventional people

definitions.text: potting Red, Green, Blue and Black?
definitions.meaning: second, cryptic meaning: in snooker these balls are worth 1, 3, 5 and 7 points, all odd numbers

explanation.surface: A snooker commentator remarks on a strange choice of shots at the table.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker scores red 1, green 3, blue 5 and black 7, so the balls named are exactly the odd-valued ones.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddball is a person with peculiar habits, someone who behaves eccentrically.

clue.text: A sailor welcomes monarch to a Middle Eastern port

indicators.note: the sailor welcomes, or takes in, the monarch's letter

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor
Q stands for queen, a monarch

explanation.surface: A sailor greets a king or queen arriving at a port in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: Q goes between A and AB, then the final A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Aqaba is Jordan's only seaport, on the Gulf of Aqaba off the Red Sea.

clue.text: Having pocketed ring, Maud fell awkwardly on forest floor, it appears

indicators.note: the rearranged letters have pocketed, or enclosed, the ring
awkwardly says the letters of Maud fell land in an ungainly new order

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Maud tumbled clumsily in the woods, having slipped a ring in her pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' turns MAUDFELL into LEAFMULD, and 'Having pocketed' puts O inside it after M.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaf mould is decayed fallen foliage, the compost-like layer that builds up under woodland trees.

clue.text: Unlucky old men lie badly

indicators.note: badly says the letters of old men lie come out in a poor, disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: Elderly men who tell bad lies tend to get caught out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ill-omened carries a bad sign of what is to come, so it is unlucky or doomed.

clue.text: Stop that man going inside: needs to be sent back for therapy

indicators.note: being sent back means the whole construction is written in reverse
the word for that man goes inside the word for stop

parts.note: to bar is to stop or block
he is the pronoun for that man

explanation.surface: A bouncer bars a man from entering a clinic and turns him away.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is short for rehabilitation, a course of treatment for addiction or injury.

clue.text: We're not done yet! Unusually flat and very hot, telling it as it is

indicators.note: unusually says these twenty-nine letters are put in an unusual new order

parts.words: flat and very hot, telling it as it is

explanation.surface: A frank weather forecaster insists the flat, scorching heatwave isn't finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase is an anagram of the twenty-nine letters of 'flat and very hot telling it as it is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying warns that an outcome is not settled until the very end, as an opera ends with a soprano's aria.

clue.text: Giants, in the main, take on girls anyhow (not good!)

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old way, so the letters are rearranged
not tells us the good letter is taken away from the pool

explanation.surface: Giant men at sea taking on women in a careless fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove G from TAKEONGIRLS and rearrange what is left. 'The main' is an old word for the open sea, so these giants are huge ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil tankers are among the largest vessels afloat, giant ships on the open ocean.

clue.text: See 13
Fashionable but not quite cool clothing: rising inflation involved here

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means this part reads upwards, reversed
the shortened word for cool goes round, clothing, the word but
not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: serene means calm, cool

explanation.surface: A trendy outfit that isn't quite cool, with rising prices playing a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inflation' looks economic, following 'rising', but it means pumping up with air, which is what happens to these rubber rings inside tyres.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner tubes sit inside tyres and are pumped full of air, so inflation in the sense of filling with air happens there.

clue.text: See 13
Half-hidden story about glands

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned about into a new order
half here keeps only the first half of the word hidden, dropping its second three letters

explanation.surface: A tale about the body's glands that is only partly concealed.
explanation.definitionFit: The thyroid is an endocrine organ in the neck that produces hormones; thyroids are such glands.

clue.text: Box set in disarray following investigation? Not right!

indicators.note: following puts the jumbled set after the shortened investigation
not means the letter for right is left out

parts.note: a search is an investigation

indicators.note: in disarray says the letters of set are jumbled

explanation.surface: A boxed TV series left in a mess after a police search.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box set' reads as a DVD collection, but 'Box' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea chest is a sailor's storage trunk, a sturdy wooden box for belongings aboard ship.

clue.text: Put it back on, you old monster!

indicators.note: in an across clue, on places the reversed it after ye

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

indicators.note: back means the word it is written backwards

explanation.surface: Telling an elderly brute to get dressed again.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti is the legendary abominable snowman said to roam the Himalayas, a mythical beast.

clue.text: Saint nearly enrols helper from the East, for this kind of treatment

indicators.note: the shortened saint enrols, or takes in, the reversed helper
nearly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Saint Patrick, the patron saint of Ireland

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means reading right to left, reversed

parts.note: an aide is a helper or assistant

explanation.surface: A saint signs up an assistant from Asia to help with patients.
explanation.walkthrough: Any saint could do; 'nearly' points to Patrick losing his K.
explanation.definitionFit: Paediatric medicine is the branch dealing with children, describing one kind of medical care.

clue.text: Spoil function supported by clique

indicators.note: in a down clue, being supported by means sitting above, so the clique comes under the function

parts.note: cos is the abbreviation for cosine, a trigonometric function
a set is a clique, a social group

explanation.surface: A party spoilt, though a circle of friends backs it.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to pamper or indulge someone, which is to spoil them.

clue.text: Literary brothers resolute at hearing

indicators.note: at a hearing things are spoken, so the word for resolute is heard rather than seen

parts.note: grim means stern, resolute

explanation.surface: Two famous writing siblings stand firm at a court hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm were the German brothers who collected and published folk tales.

clue.text: Shrub pruned more sheltered

indicators.note: pruned means cut back, so the first letter is lopped off

parts.note: cosier means snugger, more sheltered

explanation.surface: A cut-back bush is more protected from the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The osier is a willow shrub whose flexible stems are used in basketwork.

clue.text: Terrible ruler losing head in bed

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a divan is a kind of bed

explanation.surface: An awful king loses his head while lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan the Terrible was the first Tsar of Russia, a ruler famous for his cruelty.

clue.text: At sea, punishes Klaus, on vacation, netting catch of fish

indicators.note: netting means catching in a net, so the outer letters hold the catch
on vacation means emptied, leaving just the first and last letters

parts.note: an eel haul is a haul, or catch, of eels, a kind of fish

explanation.surface: Klaus, away on holiday, lands a catch while on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To keelhaul is the old naval punishment of dragging an offender under a ship's keel.

clue.text: Some verse chosen for reflection

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few lines of poetry picked out for quiet contemplation.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is sound reflected back off a surface, so it is a reflection of sound.

clue.text: Music for funeral procession bishop possibly holds each month

indicators.note: the bishop's letters hold the abbreviation for each between them

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a degree a bishop might hold
March is a month

explanation.surface: A bishop holds a service every month at which solemn music is played.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead march is slow, solemn music, such as Handel's in Saul, played at funerals.

clue.text: Root weeds out

indicators.note: out says the letters of weeds are put out of order

explanation.surface: A gardener's instruction to dig up the weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: The swede is a root vegetable, a large yellow-fleshed turnip relative, known as rutabaga in America.
